chunks: And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn Amirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

When a man divorces his wife, he should divorce her while she is in a state of purity, without sexual intercourse, with witnesses. If he marries her again after that, she is considered one of the three [divorces] for him, and the first divorce is nullified. And if he divorces her twice, then refrains from her until the third menstrual period passes, she becomes definitively divorced from him by the two [divorces], and he is suiting from the suitors. If he marries her again after that, she is considered three divorces for him, and the two are nullified. And if he divorces her three times during the waiting period, she does not become permissible to him 'until she marries another husband'.

So the beginning of what is in this narration is that it is suspended (mawquf) and not attached (musnad), because Abdullah ibn Sinan did not attach it to any of the Imams (peace be upon them). And if the matter is thus, it is permissible that he said it by his own opinion, just as Abdullah ibn Bukayr said, or that Abdullah ibn Sinan took it from Abdullah ibn Bukayr and gave fatwa with it as he heard it. And if this is probable, it is not objected to with it against what preceded from the narrations, except that this report was narrated by:

key_terms.طُهْر: Purity (state of not being in menstruation)
key_terms.مَوْقُوفَةٌ: Suspended narration (not attributed to the Prophet or Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying his ex-wife again after a single or double divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the jurisprudential nuance that this narration is 'mawquf' (suspended) because Abdullah ibn Sinan did not explicitly attribute it to an Imam, suggesting it may be his own ijtihad or derived from Abdullah ibn Bukayr. This distinction allows the report to coexist with other hadiths without contradiction, emphasizing the careful evaluation of narrator authority in Shia legal theory. The text reinforces the procedural requirements for talaq, such as purity from intercourse and the presence of witnesses, which are critical for the validity of the revocable divorce.
